scope: Independent review of synthetic review-controller hardening only. No actual MIP full-stack certification.

coverage.requirement: Require complete frontend, backend/Supabase, cross-layer coverage
coverage.explanation: Candidate adds requirementLayers plus full_stack_required so a request must declare at least one frontend, backend, and cross_layer label. That is label coverage only. validateRequest/validate in both modules never require a src/docs artifact for frontend, a supabase/(functions|migrations|qualification) artifact for backend/Supabase, or a tests artifact for cross-layer, and never require coverage.references to match the declared layer. The candidate controller fixture is already a passing three-layer PASS whose evidence is only packet:<hex>/e1..e3. Protocol's happy-path trio (src/example.jsx, supabase/migrations/..., tests/cross-layer.txt) is coincidental fixture data, not an invariant.

coverage.requirement: Allow only bounded Supabase evidence paths
coverage.explanation: Relative to base, protocol.mjs:validate:L11 is the only file-path gate. It still allows docs|tests|src|verifier, and newly allows only supabase/functions|migrations|qualification with no empty/dot-dot/dotfile segments and no trailing /AGENTS.md. supabase/.env is rejected by that regex (covered by the named test). This requirement is a restriction on Supabase paths, not a requirement that backend evidence be Supabase; controller.mjs has no filesystem paths. Residual exclusion breadth is recorded as a test gap, not a regex bypass visible in the candidate.

Controller still requires frozen 40-hex candidate, 64-hex packet, report_binding of requestKey/candidate/packet/reviewer/model, and byte-exact request/ and result/ rows. Protocol still requires frozen candidate, file byte/sha256 binding, origin.packet digest, and result.packet/candidate/request. Candidate additionally binds authority.requirements and authority.requirementLayers in disclosure_unbound (protocol.mjs:validate:L7), which base did not. No introduced unbinding of candidate, packet digest, or reserved request bytes was found.

coverage.requirement: Preserve PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED semantics and complete concrete findings
evidence_refs: verifier/review-handoff/controller.test.mjs:FAIL preserves actionable findings and proposes remediation
coverage.explanation: Controller false_pass/unsupported_fail/unsupported_blocked and structured finding fields (id, requirement, severity, summary, evidence, remediation) are unchanged from base and still required for FAIL. Intermediate run 34829897401 failed those controller tests with error 'finding'/'blocker' at controller.mjs:L37/L42; candidate tests retarget requirement frontend_behavior and corrected run 34829990489 records those tests ok. Protocol still distinguishes the three outcomes but never required concrete finding objects in base or candidate; that gap is pre-existing and not treated as a regression of this preserve-contract.

coverage.requirement: Preserve immutable requests/results and reject self-approval
evidence_refs: verifier/review-handoff/controller.test.mjs:synthetic PASS never approves merges or publishes
verifier/review-handoff/protocol.test.mjs:exact retry preserves evidence; conflicting result cannot overwrite
coverage.explanation: Controller still rejects implementer===reviewer, unknown approve/verified fields, and non-exact request/result replacement; validateReport always returns merge/approve/publish false. Protocol still rejects self/wrong reviewer, always returns merge/approve false and action synthetic_only, and receive still putOnce-keys the result. Exact retry vs conflicting overwrite remains tested. Pre-existing protocol schema looseness (extra stored fields) is a relevant residual, not an introduced self-approval return path.

synthetic===true remains mandatory on controller requests/reports and protocol packets. accept still requires transport.kind==='synthetic-test-double' and rejects {verified:true} without that kind (real_transport_disabled). Protocol still throws real_transport_not_configured when packet.synthetic!==true and never returns a non-synthetic_only action. No candidate path was found that enables merge/approve/publish or a non-synthetic transport.

coverage.requirement: Inspect failed and corrected CI evidence; identify material test gaps
coverage.explanation: Both public logs were inspected as artifacts; this reviewer did not execute tests. Failed run 34829897401 checked out a500ef1bd51c5ca1419fdac501b5057dc3b1cd81 (not the frozen candidate), 61 tests / 50 pass / 11 fail: controller FAIL/blocker cases (ok 22-29 not ok) plus protocol missing-layer cases throwing unverified_origin instead of full_stack_required (ok 46-48 not ok). Corrected run 34829990489 checked out c6dd9ed689f51d90c54f9319a9ea3fa92f389fbd, 61/61 pass. Passing counts are not treated as correctness proof. Material remaining gaps: no test that backend/Supabase layer evidence must be a bounded supabase path; protocol layer tests only rehash origin so full_stack_required is reached; supabase exclusion names 'config' but only uses supabase/.env; protocol FAIL still asserts unstructured string findings. Those gaps leave requirement 1 untested.

findings.description: Full-stack hardening is label-only. A synthetic PASS can declare backend_contract/cross_layer_semantics without any Supabase or cross-layer artifact, so the new full_stack_required check does not implement complete frontend, backend/Supabase, and cross-layer coverage.
findings.counterexample: controller.test.mjs fixture builds requirements frontend_behavior/backend_contract/cross_layer_semantics with matching requirementLayers, coverage status PASS, evidenceClass artifact_inspection, and references packet:<64 hex>/e1..e3 only. validateReport(q,r) follows controller.mjs:L18 full_stack_required then L31 unsupported_pass (packet refs, not paths) and returns outcome PASS. protocol.mjs:validate:L23-L30 likewise accepts three src/* files labeled frontend/backend/cross_layer as long as hashes, authority clones, and origin.packet digest match; no check that a backend row references supabase/(functions|migrations|qualification)/.
findings.remediation: Bind each requirementLayers value to evidence class: protocol must require at least one allowed src|docs path for frontend, one supabase/(functions|migrations|qualification)/ path for backend, and one tests/ path for cross_layer, and each PASS coverage row must reference a path in its layer's prefix set. Do not treat controller packet:<digest>/<id> tokens as satisfying backend/Supabase coverage.

findings.description: Candidate tests never attempt a three-layer PASS whose files/references omit supabase paths or point a backend requirement at a frontend path. Protocol's src + supabase/migrations + tests trio is fixture coincidence. Green node --test therefore cannot corroborate requirement 1.
findings.counterexample: controller tests 'missing frontend/backend/cross-layer coverage' only relabel requirementLayers and assert throw; they still use packet:.../e* references. protocol tests 'missing frontend/backend/cross layer' relabel layers and refresh packet/origin hashes to expect full_stack_required; they do not drop supabase/migrations/20260914000000_synthetic.sql while keeping backend_contract. No test asserts validate(...) throws when requirementLayers.backend_contract==='backend' but coverage references only src/example.jsx.
findings.remediation: Add negative tests: (1) backend layer present, zero supabase/* files, expect reject; (2) backend coverage references src/example.jsx only, expect reject; (3) cross_layer coverage references only src or supabase paths, expect reject. Keep those tests independent of origin digest mistakes.

findings.description: Failed public check log is not the frozen candidate; corrected log is 61/61 after test alignment, not after adding layer-evidence assertions. Implementer-facing pass counts are not proof the seven-requirement contract holds.
findings.counterexample: run 34829897401 job 103930505701: git rev-parse a500ef1bd51c5ca1419fdac501b5057dc3b1cd81; # fail 11 (controller tests 22-29 error finding/blocker; protocol tests 46-48 expected /full_stack_required/ got unverified_origin at protocol.mjs:L16). run 34829990489 job 103930812554: git rev-parse c6dd9ed689f51d90c54f9319a9ea3fa92f389fbd; # pass 61 # fail 0. Candidate protocol layer mutators now set a[3].packet=a[4].packet=hash(JSON.stringify(a[0])) so the origin check no longer masks full_stack_required. That makes the old failures green without testing supabase/backend evidence binding.
evidence_refs: verifier/review-handoff/controller.test.mjs:FAIL preserves actionable findings and proposes remediation
findings.remediation: Treat 34829897401 as evidence of an intermediate SHA only. Gate this PR on tests that would still fail c6dd9ed if backend/Supabase evidence can be omitted, regardless of 61/61.

findings.description: protocol.mjs still accepts FAIL/BLOCKED with non-concrete findings/blockers (any non-empty array). That is unchanged from base and still encoded as success in protocol tests, so protocol does not enforce complete concrete findings even though controller.mjs does.
findings.counterexample: protocol.test.mjs 'FAIL and BLOCKED remain distinct' sets result.findings=['synthetic-defect'] and later result.blockers=['owner_decision'] with coverage status FAIL then BLOCKED. protocol.mjs:validate:L32 only require(Array.isArray(result.findings) && Array.isArray(result.blockers)); L34 only require findings.length>0. validate(... ) returns outcome FAIL/BLOCKED. An empty object [{}] would also satisfy length>0.
findings.remediation: If protocol remains a public handoff validator, apply the same finding/blocker object schema and evidence-binding as controller validateReport. Until then, do not cite protocol FAIL as preserving concrete findings.

findings.description: protocol.mjs has no exact-key schema on result/origin/packet. Extra keys such as approve/merge/verified survive validate and are persisted by receive putOnce, even though the function return hard-codes approve/merge false. Controller rejects unknown result fields; protocol does not.
findings.counterexample: A result equal to the protocol fixture plus approve:true and merge:true still has only the checked fields used by protocol.mjs:validate:L17-L36, so validate returns {outcome:'PASS',action:'synthetic_only',merge:false,approve:false} while receive stores JSON.stringify(result) including approve/merge true under result.request. Base protocol.test.mjs also lacked an unknown-result-fields case; candidate did not add one.
findings.remediation: Reject unknown keys on protocol packet/authority/result/origin (same obj() tightness as controller) before putOnce, or persist the returned decision instead of the caller-supplied result object.

findings.description: Bounded-Supabase negatives are narrower than the test name. Only supabase/.env is attempted; supabase/config.toml, supabase/seed.sql, and a positive supabase/functions or supabase/qualification path are untested. Inspection of L11 still rejects those config/seed paths; this is coverage weakness, not a demonstrated allowlist bypass.
findings.counterexample: protocol.test.mjs 'supabase secret/config excluded' sets files[1].path='supabase/.env' and expects unsafe_path. It does not set supabase/config.toml or supabase/seed.sql. Fixture allows supabase/migrations/20260914000000_synthetic.sql but never constructs supabase/functions/... or supabase/qualification/...
findings.remediation: Assert unsafe_path for supabase/config.toml, supabase/seed.sql, and supabase/functions/../.env-style traversal; assert allow for one functions and one qualification path inside the existing charset/dot-segment rules.

limitations: Artifact inspection of the embedded packet only; no repository access, no clone, no MCP, no Supabase, no credentials, no browser, no code execution, and no independent recomputation of blob_sha or packet_sha256.
Did not execute node --test; CI conclusions cite run 34829897401 / job 103930505701 and run 34829990489 / job 103930812554 as supplied logs only. Failed log SHA a500ef1 is not the frozen candidate.

Not MIP frontend/backend product certification. Out-of-scope Stage2 items noted but not scored as this PR's introduced defects: protocol.receive putOnce crash-recovery parity with controller.accept, protocol exact-key schema (related residual f5), trusted store/transport adapters, and real wakeup/GitHub activation wiring.
This outcome has no merge, approval, publication, or production authority.
summary: FAIL for synthetic review-controller hardening at c6dd9ed versus 4b11134: complete frontend/backend-Supabase/cross-layer coverage is not enforced beyond requirementLayers labels, and the controller fixture already PASSes backend_contract with only packet token references. Real activation remains fail-closed, candidate/authority/result binding is preserved and slightly tightened, controller PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED plus structured findings are preserved, and supabase path allowlisting is bounded in protocol.mjs:L11. Failed check 34829897401 ran a500ef1 (11 fails); corrected check 34829990489 ran c6dd9ed (61/61) after fixture/digest alignment, which does not prove requirement 1. Pre-existing protocol unstructured findings and extra stored result keys remain relevant residuals, not this review's approval path.
